insight.title: Whales Sleep Standing Up
insight.subtitle: Instead of lying down, the world’s largest predators nap by bobbing vertically like giant, silent pillars.

sections.text: Sperm whales don't drift horizontally when they rest. Instead, they tilt vertically, shut down their brains, and hang motionless in the deep water like giant, floating telephone poles.
They do this in groups, hovering just beneath the surface for about fifteen minutes at a time. It’s the shortest sleep cycle of any mammal, and they remain completely unresponsive the entire time.
If you sailed over them, you’d peer down into the dark water only to find dozens of sixty-ton predators suspended upright, staring straight up at your boat, utterly unconscious.
It’s less of a bedtime, more of an underwater parking lot.
